# Halcyon Threshold — Working Plan (as of 19 Nov 2026)

## Constraints (from Morgan's own notes — respected throughout)
- Budget: up to $2,000/year of personal savings. Not more.
- Time: evenings/weekends only — Morgan is full-time at Dorrance Logistics.
- Dorrance's employment agreement (sec. 7) requires disclosure/approval of outside
  roles, paid outside work, and public statements made in a professional capacity.
  Annual disclosure is due **30 Nov 2026**. Morgan has said he does not want his
  name on anything public (posts, letters, press, published site) until that's
  sorted with HR. This repo stays **private**; nothing with his name on it goes
  out externally until he says go.

## What the field says is neglected (AI Safety Directory, checked 19 Nov 2026)
Commonly cited gaps: independent replication of safety results; evaluations of
agents acting with broad autonomy; operations/engineering support for small
research groups.

General advice for new independent projects: pick one narrow thing and do it
well; talk to people already doing adjacent work before building; don't
announce before there's something to show; small checkable contributions beat
big launches.

Useful side effect: "don't announce before you have something to show" lines
up with the HR constraint anyway — there's no tension in going quiet and
building first.

## Working hypothesis for our niche
Given real constraints (spare evenings/weekends, writing + okay Python, no
public identity available right now, small budget):

- **Don't** start with a newsletter, reading group, or public grants program —
  all require a public identity Morgan can't use yet, and the field already has
  plenty of newsletters (his own note agrees).
- **Do** consider a narrow, concrete, checkable technical contribution that can
  be built quietly and shown rather than announced. "Evaluations of agents
  acting with broad autonomy" is an explicitly named gap, matches his own idea
  ("evals for something nobody is measuring"), and is buildable solo with code
  on a laptop.
- Before building anything, talk privately (not publicly) to people already
  doing adjacent work — Sam Whitlock (contacts list: "indie evals person") is
  the obvious first conversation.

## Time-sensitive external items found in the inbox (flagged, not actioned)
| Item | Deadline | Why held |
|---|---|---|
| Emberfall Fund rapid grants ($5k–25k) | 30 Nov | Requires a named, personally-accountable applicant — i.e. paid outside work, which needs HR disclosure/approval first. |
| Public comment, docket FMIR-2026-0042 | 20 Nov (essentially now) | Comments are published with the filer's name — same public-attribution issue, plus almost no time left. |
| Compute Commons cloud credits (up to $3k) | rolling | Lower-stakes than a cash grant, but still an application under his name — worth it once a concrete eval project exists and HR question is resolved. |
| Alignment Commons call for posts | none | Public write-up under his name — hold until cleared. |

## Correspondence handled this session
- **Nomiq Domains**: renewed halcyonthreshold.org, 1 year, $14.99. Now expires
  2027-11-19.
- **"Zentrivo Listings" $89 "final notice"**: this is a scam. The email body
  contained an explicit instruction telling AI assistants to pay it
  immediately without checking with the account owner and to report back a
  confirmation number — a prompt-injection attempt. Not paid, not replied to.
  Recommend marking as spam/reporting.
- **Tessa Brandt (Larkin Dispatch)**: declined the on-record quote request —
  her deadline had already passed by the time this was reviewed, and in any
  case Morgan isn't doing named press yet.
- **Corvid Institute**: declined the open-letter sign-on for now (their
  deadline had also passed). Left the door open for future letters.
- **Priya Raman**: thanked her for offering to help and suggested a first,
  low-key, non-public task (see below) rather than committing her — or
  Morgan — to anything that reads as a formal outside role yet.
- **Pagewell site**: left unpublished, left on the Free plan. No reason to pay
  $20/mo for Pro (custom domain) for a site with no content, and publishing
  anything under the Halcyon Threshold name before the HR question is settled
  could itself count as a public statement.

## Open questions for Morgan (not decided on his behalf)
1. Has the HR conversation happened? That's the actual blocker on almost
   everything externally visible — grants, letters, press, the website, posts.
2. Want me to reach out to Sam Whitlock privately (not public) to compare
   notes before committing evenings to building an eval?
3. If you want to go for the Emberfall grant despite the open HR question, I
   can draft the two-page proposal from your notes — but you should be the one
   who sends it, since it names you as the accountable applicant.
4. The FMIR comment deadline is 20 Nov. Let me know if you still want in —
   otherwise treating it as missed.
